reply_text:
I found no dated AI prediction from Sam Altman made in 2016. I ran all three fixed searches and used all 12 searches and all 6 page openings.

- **The main 2016 source didn't open.** The likeliest place for his own words that year is Tad Friend's New Yorker profile, "Sam Altman's Manifest Destiny" (October 2016). Two tries at the New Yorker page were refused by the fetch tool, and a third was blocked as a disallowed address. The Scribd copy only loaded a "JavaScript is disabled" page.
- **A partial copy had nothing dated.** Daring Fireball quotes two paragraphs of the profile. In them, Altman talks about neural networks and how long human babies take to learn. The article itself says OpenAI's longer-term goal is a general AI that can pass the Turing test, but gives no date. I haven't read the rest of the profile, so I can't rule it out. A search snippet hinted at a passage about humans and AI merging, but I never saw it on an opened page.
- **His own 2016 post has no AI prediction.** "Moving Forward on Basic Income" (Y Combinator blog, 31 May 2016, signed by Elizabeth Rhodes, Matt Krisiloff and Altman) mentions "a world where technology replaces existing jobs" without a date. It isn't about AI arriving, so it doesn't count.
- **The searches mostly returned 2024–2026 coverage.** That includes his "by 2030" superintelligence remarks. One Substack audit quotes him saying "5 years, give or take…" but the year isn't shown, and I didn't open it.

Still unchecked from 2016: the full New Yorker profile (worth reading directly), the 27 June 2016 Bloomberg Beta panel on basic income with Andy Stern and Natalie Foster, and his 2016 posts on blog.samaltman.com.
